source_excerpts.text:
## 1. New physical interface

Keep the reciprocal passive source

\[
S=\begin{pmatrix}S_0&t\\t^T&s\end{pmatrix},\quad S^*S\preceq I,
\qquad T_z=S_0+\frac{z}{1-sz}tt^T.
\]

A calibrated reciprocal launcher sends `u`, `||u||<=1`, and its same source port receives

\[
h_z(u)=u^T T_z u=h_0(u)+\frac{z}{1-sz}a(u),
\quad a(u)=(t^T u)^2,
\quad p(u)=|a(u)|.
\]

The transpose is essential. A generic receiver projection does not have this identity. A reciprocal matched multiport launcher with unused source ports terminated provides an ideal realization. Mismatch, residual reflection, insertion loss and unequal transmit/receive transfer must be calibrated or enclosed. A reference is added downstream and isolated from the specimen; reference leakage changes the model unless bounded.

Only the target states `0,+r,-r`, `0<r<1`, are needed. In an ideal real reference impedance these are resistances `Z0`, `Z0(1+r)/(1-r)`, `Z0(1-r)/(1+r)`, hence `Z0,3Z0,Z0/3` for `r=1/2`. Switch and line parasitics must be calibrated at the target reference plane; state labels are not calibration.

source_excerpts.text:
## Reciprocal one-feed collection

For a reflectionless reciprocal mesh, the forward/reverse matrices are U,U^T.
Its full scattering [[0,U^T],[U,0]] is symmetric and unitary for unitary U.
Drive feed e1, prepare u=Ue1 and match all unused feed ports. The returning
field T(z)u reaches the same feed as u^T T(z)u. A calibrated directional
separator and a passive 50:50 reference combiner feed one power detector.
Other return modes are dumped, not falsely counted as measured total power.
The separator must not introduce an unmodelled loop; insertion loss, leakage,
detector gain and incident normalization are calibrated or bounded.

There is a stronger per-configuration observation: **any fixed passive
reciprocal front end** with one source/return feed, one tagged target and all
other ports matched reduces to a reciprocal two-port plus loss. Its scalar
return is beta+z a/(1-s_eff z), with a=h^2, where |h|^2 is the actual matched
target power per upstream feed power. Thus front-end reciprocal insertion
loss/reflections do not require knowing microscopic parameters for this
per-configuration metrology. However, changing unknown reflections with the
command can change the effective source: the O(n) fixed-Gram control theorem
still requires a calibrated fixed linear mode map or a justified perturbation
bound. It cannot treat arbitrary programmable cavities as a fixed input basis.

## A. Reciprocal collection and actual acquired information

For a fixed reciprocal passive source, a reciprocal launcher with forward U
and reverse transpose U^T returns u^T T_z u through its driven feed. Its target
residue is (t^T u)^2, whose magnitude equals matched-target power. The Schur
complement of the hidden load yields T_z=S0+z tt^T/(1-sz); |s|<=1 and |z|<1
make the denominator nonzero. A fixed reciprocal lossy front end can be reduced
to a passive reciprocal two-port for each configuration. This per-configuration
identity does not prove that arbitrary changing front ends share one fixed Gram.
Control needs an actual fixed calibrated linear command map and source.

Expanding half-combined powers gives I0-Ipi=2R Re h and
Ipi/2-I3pi/2=2R Im h. Four absolute errors bounded by eta give independent
quadrature bounds eta/R and hence field error sqrt(2)eta/R. Twelve powers
acquire the three fields. These are additional interference observations;
intensity-only square-root lower bounds retain their original scope. Reference
power, combiner loss, detector dynamic range and all calibration are charged.

statement: For a fixed passive reciprocal source and reciprocal launcher,its same-feed return is h_z(u)=h0(u)+z a(u)/(1-sz),a(u)=(t^T u)^2 and |a(u)|=p(u). A fixed reciprocal lossy front end gives the same per-configuration two-port residue identity.
